title: Role-play lab: six step-up conversations
objectives: Handle six realistic step-up conversations: check, illustrate, set up, record.
Keep every projection illustrative and every commitment bounded.
body_md:
Practise these in pairs, five minutes each. The expected answer is the shape of a good conversation, not a script.

## 1. The new graduate

Riya, 24, can invest ₹5,000 a month but expects 10% yearly raises. Expected: suggest a 10% step-up timed to her raise; check her emergency fund first.

## 2. The ₹1 crore goal

Karan wants ₹1 crore in 15 years but can afford only ₹12,000 a month now. Expected: show the step-up path (about ₹11,500 to start with 10% a year, illustrative); no promises.

## 3. "Next year"

Sameer has said he'll increase his SIP "next year" for three years running. Expected: show the cost of delay; set an automatic step-up with a cap.

## 4. Pay cut

Anita's step-up is due but her salary was cut 15%. Expected: hold or reduce the step-up; don't cancel the SIP; review in six months.

## 5. Existing SIP

Vivek wants to add a step-up to a 4-year-old SIP. Expected: check whether it needs re-registration and any exit-load change; offer a second SIP as an alternative.

## 6. Big bonus

Meghna got a ₹4 lakh bonus. Expected: emergency fund first, then a lump sum or STP, plus a modest step-up.
example: In the Vivek role-play, the good answer covers three things: whether the AMC allows the facility on an existing SIP, what re-registration does to the instalment and exit-load clock, and the second-SIP alternative.
say: Let's see whether your AMC allows a step-up on this SIP, or whether a second SIP is cleaner.
We'll set a cap so this stays comfortable.
never: We'll just convert it; nothing changes.

talk_track.title: Practise before you need it
talk_track.text: To wrap up: practise this before you need it. Role-play the six client scenarios from the manual in pairs, take the twenty-five question quiz, where the pass mark is twenty, and use the thirty-two flash cards for quick revision. All figures are illustrative, and fund house terms vary, so always check the scheme form.

check.q: Riya, 24, can invest ₹5,000 a month and expects 10% raises. What is the best plan?
o: A 10% step-up timed to her raise, after checking her emergency fund
check.why: A step-up at her expected income growth, timed to the raise, with the buffer checked first.

check.q: Karan can afford ₹12,000 a month now but wants ₹1 crore in 15 years. What do you show?
o: The illustrative step-up path (about ₹11,500 to start at 10% a year), with assumptions and no promises
That a flat SIP will do
That he should borrow to invest more
check.why: Show the illustrative path and its assumptions, and label it clearly.

check.q: Vivek wants to add a step-up to a 4-year-old SIP. What must be checked?
o: Whether the AMC allows it on an existing SIP, and what re-registration does to the instalment and exit-load clock
Whether the SIP can be cancelled first
check.why: Check the facility and the re-registration effects, and offer a second SIP as an alternative.
